version.changelog:
Major update: Version 2.0.0 introduces a comprehensive overhaul based on real thesis review experience.

- Redesigned review framework, structured by actual review experience from 13 master theses.
- Added detailed step-by-step review workflow covering information extraction, content analysis, literature comparison, and opinion generation.
- Included standardized review templates, innovation evaluation criteria, and common issues based on statistics.
- Introduced Word document output with specific formatting requirements.
- Enabled support for batch thesis review and comparative reporting.
- Expanded documentation with usage scenarios, file explanations, and version history.

llm.summary: This is a coherent thesis-review helper that reads user-provided thesis PDFs and generates review documents, with privacy considerations users should manage.

dimensions.detail: The PDF text extraction, literature comparison, review rubric, and Word document generation all fit the stated academic thesis review purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Some trigger phrases are broad academic terms, so users should invoke it intentionally for thesis review rather than general writing feedback.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a manifest and SKILL.md; no executable install scripts, hidden binaries, or automatic setup behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Using local PDF parsing and public web search for recent literature is proportionate to evaluating thesis novelty and quality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs generation of .docx review files and references historical review archives, but this is disclosed and aligned with its purpose; it does not request background persistence or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the agent process thesis PDFs and create review documents that may include personal and unpublished academic information. For blind review or confidential theses, remove identifying details first and avoid saving or sharing generated documents outside the approved review process.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Broad review-related triggers are real but not evidence of hidden or unsafe behavior; intentional invocation is advisable.
[SQP-2] expected: Extracting author, school, academic results, and project history is part of the review workflow, but users should handle unpublished or blind-review theses as confidential.
